target_customer: Developers and companies building fast-growing web and mobile apps that need a managed, globally distributed NoSQL database
problem: Scaling and operating a distributed database is hard for small app teams. Cloudant ran and scaled CouchDB-style data stores as a service.

founders.name: Michael Miller
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: recovering particle physicist and distributed systems developer. Education and employers not given on the page.

founders.name: Alan Hoffman
founders.background_notes: YC page describes the company as founded by three MIT physicists; no individual bio.

founders.name: Adam Kocoloski
founders.background_notes: YC page describes the company as founded by three MIT physicists; no individual bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a fault-tolerant, globally distributed data layer on CouchDB (later released as BigCouch) required distributed systems expertise that most small teams lacked in 2008.

defensibility.rationale: Operating distributed database clusters at scale and customer data lock-in gave some protection, but the underlying CouchDB code was open source and BigCouch was released under Apache License 2.0 in August 2010.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: IBM acquired Cloudant, announced 2014-02-24, to extend its cloud portfolio after buying SoftLayer. TechCrunch named MongoDB as a competing alternative at that point.

market_need_then: Founders came from large-scale physics data work (multi-petabyte LHC data per the YC page) and were frustrated with the tools available for managing big data. Web and mobile developers wanted databases that scale without in-house operations.

branding.domain_note: Used cloudant.com; no acquisition story found.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: YC description is casual and developer friendly (sleep more knowing we're keeping the servers up)

rebrands.why: Became an IBM product after the acquisition; cloudant.com now redirects to ibm.com/cloud/cloudant.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within the CouchDB and developer community, but no source shows press about the brand itself, merch or community rituals.

outcome_analysis: Cloudant started in the YC Summer 2008 batch with physicist founders who had handled huge data sets, built a distributed layer on CouchDB, and raised about $15.1 million in total by 2014 according to TechCrunch. The rise of mobile and web apps and the shift to managed cloud data created demand, and IBM bought the company in February 2014 for an undisclosed price to bolster its cloud portfolio after SoftLayer.
notes: Company site redirects to IBM (cloudant.com to ibm.com/cloud/cloudant). No dated 2008 competitor sources found, so the list is empty. Total raised conflicts: 15.1M (TechCrunch) versus about 14M (SoCal Tech, CB Insights). An aggregator lists a 1M Series A from Avalon in 2011 and further 2012 and 2013 rounds; unverified by a primary source and not recorded as rounds. Aggregator claim of a former name 26 Solutions is unverified.
